bottom_line: Lenient versus strict rate control in permanent atrial fibrillation was noninferior for the primary composite outcome at 3 years (12.9% vs. 14.9%; absolute difference, −2.0 percentage points; 90% CI, −7.6 to 3.5).
implications: At 3 years, these data support that lenient rate control is noninferior to strict rate control for the reported composite primary outcome (12.9% vs. 14.9%; absolute difference −2.0 percentage points; 90% CI, −7.6 to 3.5; hazard ratio 0.84 [90% CI, 0.58–1.21]) and that target attainment was higher with fewer visits (97.7% vs. 67.0%; 75 vs. 684 total visits). The trial does not establish superiority of either strategy because the primary analysis is framed as noninferiority and the confidence interval includes no difference.

major_points.text: Randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial comparing lenient vs strict rate-control strategies in permanent atrial fibrillation.
major_points.quote: The Rate Control Efficacy in Permanent Atrial Fibrillation: a Comparison between Lenient versus Strict Rate Control II (RACE II) study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, HF hospitalization, and thromboembolic, bleeding, and serious arrhythmic events.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, hospitalization for heart failure, and stroke, systemic embolism, bleeding, and life-threatening arrhythmic events.

major_points.text: Heart-rate targets were achieved more often with lenient control and required fewer total visits.
major_points.quote: More patients in the lenient-control group met the heart-rate target or targets (304 [97.7%], vs. 203 [67.0%] in the strict-control group; P<0.001) with fewer total visits (75 [median, 0], vs. 684 [median, 2]; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Frequencies of symptoms and adverse events were similar between strategies.
major_points.quote: The frequencies of symptoms and adverse events were similar in the two groups.

guidelines_referenced.text: ACC/AHA/ESC 2006 Guidelines for the Management of Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/European Society of Cardiology)
guidelines_referenced.quote: ACC/AHA/ESC 2006 Guidelines for the Management of Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: a report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Practice Guidelines and the European Society of Cardiology Committee for Practice Guidelines

inclusion_criteria.text: Permanent atrial fibrillation for up to 12 months.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility criteria were as follows: permanent atrial fibrillation for up to 12 months

exclusion_criteria.quote: Thus, we excluded patients with a previous stroke, resulting in a low-risk study population.

criticisms.text: Strict-control targets were achieved in only 67.0% of patients (vs virtually always in lenient group).
criticisms.quote: In our strict-control group, the resting and exercise targets were achieved in 67.0% of the patients, whereas in the lenient- control group the target rate was virtually always

criticisms.text: Low-risk population and design choices may have contributed to a lower-than-expected event rate.
criticisms.quote: Thus, we ex- cluded patients with a previous stroke, resulting in a low-risk study population. These choices may have resulted in the lower-than-expected prima- ry outcome event rate.

criticisms.text: Potential differences in symptom severity could not be ruled out despite similar prevalence.
criticisms.quote: Although the prevalence of symptoms was similar in the two groups in our study, we cannot rule out potential differences in the severity of symptoms between the groups.
